plan.storyTreatment:
A gust of wind tipped a lantern sideways just as the first picnic basket reached the woodland entrance. The storm had passed, but leaves still skittered across the path. Four lanterns had marked the way to the night picnic. Now two glowed along the path, and the others were gone. The neighbors waited in the meadow. Moonrise would come soon.

Rabbit darted ahead. “I’ll find them all!” At the ditch, Rabbit spotted one lantern among wet leaves, lifted it, and hurried to the fork. Rabbit set it beside the wrong trail. From there, its warm light pointed away from the meadow. “One fixed!” Rabbit called, already running on.

Wise Turtle had wanted to check each lantern place in order. “We should look at every spot first,” Turtle said. But the neighbors were waiting, and Rabbit was already out of sight. Turtle followed slowly, looking closely. Beyond the fallen log, Turtle found another lantern on its east side. Rabbit’s lantern had come from the east ditch. Turtle remembered seeing Rabbit carry it from there.

Rabbit bounced back to the fork. “I found a third!” Turtle said. “Wait. The first was east of the path in the ditch. This one is east of the log. They both blew the same way.” Turtle looked toward the low stone wall farther along the path. “The last lantern may be beyond it.”

Rabbit started to sprint, then stopped. “Let’s look together.” Turtle agreed to follow the clue without checking every empty place first. They went toward the wall. Rabbit searched quickly among the leaves, while Turtle checked the ground beside the stones. There, the last lantern’s handle peeked out from behind the wall. Rabbit reached it and held it steady while Turtle eased it free.

They carried the lanterns back together. At the fork, Rabbit lifted the misplaced light and returned it to the bend where it belonged. Turtle brought the lantern from beyond the wall back to its old place. The lantern from the log went beside the log again. Rabbit checked each glow against the path, and Turtle checked that no turn pointed toward the wrong trail. This time, neither hurried past the other’s check.

The neighbors followed the lights from the entrance. Rabbit bounced ahead to welcome them, then waited at each turn. Wise Turtle walked beside the last basket and watched the path behind them. They reached the meadow before moonrise. The lanterns shone along the woods, and the picnic blankets were ready. Rabbit sat beside Turtle as the neighbors unpacked warm rolls and berries. “Next time,” Rabbit said, “I’ll look before I move the light.” Turtle smiled. “And I’ll know when a good clue is enough to begin.” Together they watched the lantern glow settle across the path.

plan.storyTreatment:
Rainwater tapped the leaves as Rabbit found a lantern rocking in the grass beside the creek-side of the hollow stump. A small storm had scattered all four lanterns from their places along the woodland path. The neighbors were waiting at the trailhead for the night picnic. They needed to reach the clearing before moonrise.

Rabbit grabbed the lantern and raced to the fern fork. “A light farther along will help,” Rabbit said, hanging it beside the wrong trail. Soon, several neighbors followed its glow down the fern lane. They soon saw there was no clearing there and turned back to wait at the trailhead. Rabbit heard their voices and hurried onward, hoping to fix the other lanterns before anyone else got confused.

At the split oak, Rabbit found another lantern resting in the grass on the creek-side. Wise Turtle caught up. Turtle had started from the trailhead with the neighbors, then followed Rabbit’s hurried tracks. “Where did the stump lantern land?” Turtle asked. Rabbit admitted it had been beside the creek, before being moved to the fork. Now they had two clues: one lantern had landed creek-side of the stump, and another creek-side of the split oak.

Wise Turtle wanted to inspect every empty lantern place before making a plan. The moonrise deadline was getting closer. Turtle looked from the remembered spot by the stump to the lantern beside the oak. “Both landed on the creek-side,” Turtle said. “The storm pushed them that way. The lantern by the bent pine may be creek-side too. So may the one by the fern arch.” Turtle chose to trust the pattern and asked Rabbit to search by the arch while Turtle checked the bent pine.

Rabbit started to dash back, then stopped. First, Rabbit carried the lantern from the fork to its proper place by the stump. Then Rabbit walked on to the fern arch, keeping the creek on the same side. There, just as Turtle predicted, another lantern lay in wet grass on the creek-side. Rabbit lifted it and returned it to the arch. At the bent pine, Turtle found the third displaced lantern and set it back in its place. At the split oak, Turtle returned the lantern Rabbit had found. One by one, the four familiar lights marked the true path again.

They went back to the trailhead. Rabbit could have raced ahead to the clearing, but instead stayed with the neighbors and waited for everyone to be ready. Wise Turtle trusted Rabbit to lead the first stretch, without checking every lantern alone. Together they guided the group past the stump, away from the fern fork, and onward from light to light. No one hurried off the path. The neighbors reached the picnic clearing before moonrise.

The group settled in as the lanterns shone behind them. Rabbit sat beside Wise Turtle and listened to the leaves drip. “The lights are easier to follow when we look together,” Rabbit said. Wise Turtle nodded. For a quiet moment, neither of them rushed to fill the night with words.
